input.prompt:
Analyze the following Gmail message context. Current datetime: 2026-06-27T16:16:24

Message 1
Date: 2024-06-01
To: 
From: teammate@corp.com
Subject: Urgent approval
Message_body: Can you approve and reply asap?
Structured_thread: Current message:
datetime: 2024-06-01
sender: teammate@corp.com
content: Can you approve and reply asap?

Previous messages: None

Output instructions:
Return plain text only.
For each input message, output exactly one line in this exact format:
priority=<low|normal|medium|high|urgent>; event_title=<none or title>; event_start=<none or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS>; event_end=<none or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS>; event_location=<none or location>
Use event fields only for upcoming calendar-worthy meetings, calls, appointments, interviews, travel reservations, deadlines, or concrete reminders. Use none for every event field when there is no upcoming concrete event.
in the same order as the input messages.
Allowed priority words: low, normal, medium, high, urgent.
Use urgent only when the latest message explicitly asks the user to reply, respond, confirm, approve, or call back immediately/asap/right away. Do not use urgent for important-looking notifications without an immediate reply request.
Use high when the latest message asks for a reply or action within a short stated window such as today, tomorrow, this week, within a few days, by a concrete date, or before a deadline.
Use medium when the latest message asks for a meaningful reply or action but gives no clear short deadline.
Use normal for ordinary useful information that does not ask the user to reply or act soon. Use low for bulk, automated, promotional, unsubscribe-style, or unlikely to require action.
Do not return JSON, labels, Gmail metadata, reasoning, markdown, or tool calls.
Do not draft a reply.

messages.subject: Urgent approval
messages.Message_body: Can you approve and reply asap?
